claims.text: Binary phase-diagram analysis can be used to predict whether high-entropy alloys form single solid-solution phases or phases containing intermetallics.
Near-equiatomic nanoparticles whose compositions fall within predicted single-phase regions preserve structural and chemical integrity during catalytic and thermoelectric service.
Predicted single-phase regions are high-configurational-entropy regimes.
An entropy-stabilized solid-solution phase suppresses phase segregation and intermetallic formation.
A homogeneous entropy-stabilized solid solution retards elemental diffusion.
High configurational entropy minimizes the thermodynamic driving force for phase segregation at high temperature.
High configurational entropy limits intermetallic nucleation at high temperature.
Shifting composition toward an intermetallic-forming region lowers an entropic barrier to atomic rearrangement.
Lowering this entropic barrier accelerates atomic rearrangements and produces chemical inhomogeneity.
Compositions shifted toward phase-diagram regions associated with intermetallics are more likely to form intermetallic-containing phase assemblages.
Optimized nanoparticles will exhibit less phase separation after thermal exposure than compositionally deviated nanoparticles.
Optimized nanoparticles will retain their morphology after high-temperature exposure.
Optimized nanoparticles will retain catalytic and thermoelectric performance after high-temperature exposure.
Off-target nanoparticles will undergo phase segregation and intermetallic formation during service exposure.
Phase segregation and intermetallic formation will reduce catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
Nanoparticles not optimized using phase-diagram guidance typically lose structural and chemical homogeneity during high-temperature service.
The proposed stabilization mechanism applies across catalytic temperatures of 773–1173 K and thermoelectric temperatures of 473–1923 K.
Outside the stated temperature ranges or under extreme composition deviations, other degradation mechanisms may predominate.
